mn63:2.2: As used here ‘world’ means the universe and even more than this as it comprises also the various sub-human and super-human states.
mn63:2.5: For preference and liking see Sutta 95 para. 14; 101, para. 11.
mn63:5.21: Renderings of akka (fibre), saṇha (reed), maruvā (hemp), and khīrapaṇṇa (bark) are guesswork. There is no reliable guidance. It is difficult to see how P.T.S. Dict. can give a botanical Latin name to khīrapaṇṇa (lit., milk-leaf), since if that identification is based on Sanskrit, it is not reliable for Sutta Pāli.
mn63:5.25: Kaṅkā—crow: see Sutta 54, para. 17, note. Sithilahanu—stork: this is a guess since P.T.S. Dict. and Comy only say ‘a kind of bird’. The name ‘loose-jaw’ could apply to certain kinds of storks or cranes whose beaks do not meet in the middle.
mn63:5.27: Comy. glosses bherava (‘lion’ here) as kāḷa-sīha (black lion), though P.T.S. Dict. gives ‘hart’.
mn63:5.29: Khurappa—hoof-tip: not in P.T.S. Dict. Vekaṇḍa—curved, nārāca—barbed, vacchadanta—lit., ‘calf’s tooth’, karavīrapaṇṇa—lit., ‘oleander-leaf’, are guesses at the meanings of these descriptions of arrowhead shapes.
mn63:8.2: Ādibrahmacariyaka—belonging to the principles of the life divine.
